Inspired by experiences of a real Dota 2 survivor, this game is kinda FUN. And even losing is fun for once. Overall picture is part awesome and part feels like a scam, it is claimed there are tons or supposedly hundreds of hidden upgrades, that could be paradoxal and derived from nerfs to stats - but in like 25.5 hours and bajillion of attempts to find them, I have found what feels like just a few (but they are so overpowered that they can beat whole game easy - so what's the point of more?) It is also comparable to Path of Exile in variety of possible ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, except you are only prevented from insanely overpowered character building by RNGesus, sometimes Good: + Skill based combat, that akin to POE becomes ultra hard and untenable without building good character, which requires smart strategy that is fun to figure (prepare to git gud) + Soundtrack by Vivaldi + Quite a lot of challenges and various runs to try, however they award no progression except personal mastery Bad: - As a game developer I would say most of practical game design is terribly lazy, kind of low effort etc. which in specific conditions is a problem and is makes it barely playable or barely visible (FPS killing from slightly too intense effect stacking or lightning from hits) - quite a bit of graphics are simply too primitive, this developer possibly has no experience at all in anything - which is better than most - There are some glitches that might be fixed in some days, but why wasn't it playtested half decently? - If you are suffering from a skill issue - then it may be really tedious and repetitive, think again about strategy and figure what is useless and what is useful - you can banish upgrade options and focus on specific ones - Apparently not much content, but seems like more is to come and it wouldn't be hard to expand on - There is only one mode now that is only playable in one sitting, which takes time - Often no explanations to mechanics and options (very much like Path of Exile indeed) - Not much to do when you get too gud It truly has potential, but it is unclear if it will be really unlocked Some tryhards are probably the target audience, but the paradox is that if you have IQ low enough to struggle forever, you will enjoy it a lot more, but will eternally struggle... Not many games are gamey like that or have potential for genuine struggle at all

Exceptionally fun game, inspired by a DotA 2 mod and brought into the roguelike genre. Just missing a few QOL features that have come to be expected in this genre: [list] [*] Codex of discovered upgrades [*] Indicator/list of banished upgrades [*] Endless mode option at the end of a run [*] Ability to hover/read upgrades while game is paused [*] Visual indication of temporary buff indication [/list] The conditional upgrades are super fun, but could use a little more intelligence. If I've banished my entire weapon or spell, I probably don't wanna see those things in the elite-shop. While this is a bit antithetical to the RNG design and could be bad for balance; this is a single player game. I don't wanna bash my head into 100 runs trying to get Spell Reflect > Vampiress, I wanna banish my entire weapon and spell to curate the elite-shop into giving me those things There's also some content that seems obvious to me but seems to have been missed by devs. There's three elements, but only spells for 2, and a lot of conditional upgrades that I would expect to find which I have not yet. Healing Rain on negative damage for example. Due to the lack of a codex, it's impossible to know if I just haven't found these or if they didn't think of them.

I think I've played this long enough to give an objective review. For this I'll be putting aside the fact I've been watching Baumi for the better part of 7 years and focus on the game itself. It's as described, you run your dude around, dodge projectiles, autoattack, and can choose a specific stat to "boost" to create your build. after a boss you get to select a special boost (think Evolution from Vamp Survs, kinda) that either changes effect or massively improves cooldown or damage. its not a revolutionary idea, but it works well in practice. i was struggling for my first few games until i got a hold of what's important and what's less important (but still maybe good memes) The gameplay loop is okay, and the upgrades are interesting and have their own flair to them. My main issue with the game is some minor bugginess, like enemies getting stuck in your character if you dash into them, or the fact that the hitbox for the player character just... feels a bit off. It's like the character's top of their head isn't there and the feet are like, 5 pixels lower than on screen. And for a game all about dodging projectiles and enemies, the movement is horrible on MnK, i highly recommend plugging in that controller, it helps a lot, but doenst mitigate the movement jank on dodges. However, this is a $.99 game, and it's extremely refreshing to see a smaller game at a smaller price. I'd rather pay .99 and have 3 hours of slightly buggy fun, seeing what BS i can pull off; as opposed to $60 in (insert AAA studio's *very* buggy game) and spend 100 hours being mostly miserable. The game runs relatively stable, I noticed one crash but that may have been due to my internet disconnecting. The only things I would change are some QOL things. The two QOL things that stood out to me were: #1 make it so if a powerup spawns behind the healthbar, it goes translucent like if an enemy, or you, are up there. And #2 some effects just dont look right and are hard to see. Acid pool does not look like acid, i could barely tell it existed, and the Twin's attacks just... didn't feel like attacks. They smacked me 3x until my brain registered what that was. But again, its .99c, I've already got my money's worth and more. So if it looks remotely interesting, give it a shot.

Pros: Simple concept. very straightforward, only $1 Cons: Game is not balanced, lots of bugs, terrible stat/skill descriptions, too slow of an early game, too much luck regarding if you get the boosts you want, lots of annoying enemies that aren't difficult so much as oversimplified. This could use a huge QOL and balance patch, and almost all of it has to do with the boosts themselves. Having 8 options per boost instead of 4 and/or having a means of generating boosts (outside of the Shovel) would really add a sense of control to the game. Banishes should probably come with a bonus - right now they feel like a burden. That being said, you can't expect that much from a $1 pet project. As such, you are better off playing many many other survivor games, even at this price point.
